facts.label: Version relationships and conflicts
facts.text: - Saxoprint: the 10-K (filed after the July 2 closing) states the price as "€120,000" in thousands, "subject to a post-closing adjustment", and that "no definitive agreement has been executed" for a sale-leaseback (pages:70, 142). The September 2026 10-Q states total purchase consideration "$141,081 (€123,996 based on the exchange rate on the acquisition date)", a plan approved to market and execute a sale-leaseback, held-for-sale assets of "$46,303" on the balance sheet, and a preliminary allocation to be finalised "during the second quarter of fiscal year 2027" (pages:18-19, 2). These are different dates of the same transaction, not a contradiction of fact. The later 10-Q controls the amount and funding (cash and the revolver, with "$35,000" of revolver borrowings, page:21). No executed sale-leaseback is evidenced. - Restated Credit Agreement: the 10-K describes a Term Loan B of "$1,097,250" at June 30, 2026 and no revolver borrowings; the 10-Q describes "$1,094,500" and revolver borrowings of "$35,000" at September 30, 2026 (page:21). Different balance sheet dates; both remain active evidence for their own dates. - Maturity: the 10-Q adds that the Term Loan B is subject to an earlier maturity of June 16, 2032 if the 2032 Notes have not been repaid, refinanced or extended as specified (page:21); the 10-K states a final maturity of June 4, 2033 (page:118). The 10-Q wording is the more complete statement of that term; the executed agreement is not supplied to confirm it. - Duplicates: none identified. No source is a hash duplicate of another.

The reported Consolidated Leverage Ratio and headroom are not printed; the test applies only if revolving usage exceeds 20% of commitments at a quarter end (page:21)

Letters of credit under the revolver are not itemised; the filing gives "available borrowing capacity ... was $197.7 million" and "$4.5 million" of lease-related bank guarantees and letters of credit (page:46)
Required principal payments by year are printed only at June 30, 2026 (page:140); at September 30, 2026 only bucketed contractual obligations are printed (page:45)
No separate discrete fourth-quarter FY2026 statement is retained; only the annual report and the first three quarterly reports
Saxoprint purchase price allocation is preliminary and no sale-leaseback agreement is evidenced
No presentations; the pack substitutes earnings releases, which are unreadable
Ratings, market quotes, peer data, deal terms and research questions are blank in the context
Image, chart and speaker-note content is not covered because the sources are text extractions
Currency and units: statements are USD in thousands; the Saxoprint price is also stated in euros; MD&A uses millions

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The financial base is adequate for downstream credit work, with stated limits. Reported statements for FY2024, FY2025, FY2026, Q1 FY2026 and Q1 FY2027 are complete and their expense blocks reconcile to operating income. On the issuer's own adjusted EBITDA, total debt to EBITDA was 3.70x at FY2025, 3.57x at FY2026 and 3.71x on the trailing twelve months to September 30, 2026; net debt to EBITDA was 3.16x, 3.03x and 3.44x. EBITDA to cash interest was 3.93x, 4.18x and 4.11x. The movement in the latest period is explained by the July 2026 Saxoprint acquisition, which was funded from cash and revolver borrowings, while trailing EBITDA contains only the post-acquisition months and Q1 FY2027 adjusted EBITDA fell year on year. In US$m: total debt principal 1,667.6, cash 120.1, liquidity 317.8 (June 30, 2026: 481.6), share-based compensation added back in FY2026 61.4, and adjusted free cash flow 122.4 in FY2026 (FY2025: 148.0). Three limits bind every metric: adjusted EBITDA is the issuer's measure and adds back share-based compensation, the covenant definition and reported ratio are not supplied, and debt excludes finance leases, supply chain finance and purchase commitments, which are shown separately.

facts.label: Credit interpretation
facts.text: - Leverage and acquisition effect. Between June 30, 2026 and September 30, 2026 debt principal rose by 31,227 thousand while cash fell by 128,724 thousand, because Saxoprint cost 131,557 thousand net of cash acquired and was funded from cash and 35,000 thousand of revolver borrowings (10-Q Sep 2026 pages:4, 21). Net leverage therefore rose to 3.44x from 3.03x, while LTM EBITDA holds only the post-acquisition part of the new business and its pre-acquisition EBITDA is not supplied. The first-quarter adjusted EBITDA decline (89,820 against 98,715) came mainly from higher start-up costs for the North American network, tariff costs and depreciation, partly offset by a 7.5 million tariff refund benefit (10-Q Sep 2026 page:33). Run-rate leverage after acquired EBITDA and any sale-leaseback proceeds cannot be derived from the sources. - Quality of EBITDA. Issuer adjusted EBITDA adds back share-based compensation (61,379 in FY2026, 13.4% of FY2026 adjusted EBITDA) and deducts realised losses on currency hedges (14,169). Treating share-based compensation as a cost gives FY2026 EBITDA of 397,119 and total leverage of 4.12x; on LTM figures 387,106 and 4.31x. The hedge programme targets adjusted EBITDA to maintain stability on debt covenants (10-Q Sep 2026 page:50), so adjusted EBITDA is plausibly close to the covenant definition, but that cannot be confirmed without the credit agreement. - Cash generation. Operating cash flow fell from 350,722 (FY2024) to 283,706 (FY2026) while capital spending, including capitalised software, rose to 167,290 in FY2026. Issuer adjusted free cash flow, which is after cash interest because operating cash flow includes interest paid (10-Q Sep 2026 page:34), fell from 261,053 to 122,432. In FY2026 cash was also used for acquisitions of 32,390, share repurchases of 50,077, withholding taxes on equity awards of 19,313 and finance lease payments of 11,740 (10-K pages:89-90). A buyback authorisation of 200 million remains (10-Q Sep 2026 page:52); none was used in Q1 FY2027, and share repurchases are restricted payments under the secured facility (10-Q Sep 2026 page:21). - Liquidity. Liquidity at September 30, 2026 was 317.8 million against 481.6 million at June 30, 2026. Contractual obligations falling due within one year total 278,887 thousand including interest, leases and purchase commitments (10-Q Sep 2026 page:45). The second fiscal quarter is the peak season; the first-quarter working capital outflow was 23.7 million (10-Q Sep 2026 page:44). - Maturities and refinancing. Scheduled amortisation is small (11.5 to 18.5 million a year), with 1,570.6 million due after FY2031. The Term Loan B springs to June 16, 2032 unless the 2032 Notes are repaid, refinanced or extended, so the practical wall is the 525.0 million note refinancing in 2032. - Debt-like claims outside the debt figure. Finance leases of 56,003, operating lease payments of 157,858 (undiscounted fixed), supply chain finance of 58,781 inside accounts payable, purchase commitments of 310,257 (cloud services 192,636), redeemable noncontrolling interests of 78,361 (a put exercised by minority holders of one small business will require 9,602 in the second quarter of FY2027), and pension liabilities of 9,060. Including finance leases, total leverage is 3.83x on LTM figures. Book equity is a deficit of 479,409 after cumulative share repurchases (treasury shares at cost 1,363,550). - Covenant. A maintenance test of Consolidated Leverage Ratio not above 4.50x applies only if revolving loans, swingline loans and unreimbursed letter of credit disbursements exceed 20% of commitments at a fiscal quarter end (10-Q Sep 2026 page:21). On the printed 35,000 of loans against 250,000 of commitments, usage was 14.0%, so the test was not triggered at September 30, 2026; 15,000 of further drawings would reach the 20% threshold. Management states compliance with all covenants (10-Q Sep 2026 page:21). The covenant ratio itself is not printed. - Data checks. Operating income reconciles to gross profit less the expense block of technology, marketing, general and administrative, intangible amortisation and restructuring for all five periods. The adjusted EBITDA bridges recompute to the printed figures. Debt principal by instrument sums to the printed total at each date.

rows.label: Leverage on the issuer's adjusted EBITDA is moderate: total debt 3.57x at FY2026 and 3.71x on the trailing twelve months to September 30, 2026, after a debt-funded acquisition. EBITDA to cash interest was 4.11x.
Total debt rose to US$1,667.6m at September 30, 2026 while cash fell to US$120.1m, mainly because of the Saxoprint purchase.
Liquidity at September 30, 2026 was US$317.8m, from US$120.1m cash and US$197.7m of revolver availability.
Adjusted EBITDA adds back US$61.4m of share-based compensation in FY2026, and adjusted free cash flow fell to US$122.4m from US$148.0m.
The covenant is a springing 4.50x leverage test that applies only when the revolver is more than 20% used at a quarter end.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Cimpress is a decentralised group of web-to-print and promotional-product businesses run by a small central team, financed with a covenant-light structure of a secured term loan and revolver plus unsecured notes. The creditor-relevant business facts are that one brand, VistaPrint, supplies most segment EBITDA with high gross margin and low working capital; that the Upload and Print segments earn lower margins but are growing faster and are the acquisition platform; that profits are concentrated in the December quarter; and that U.S. tariffs, energy and North American capacity start-up costs are compressing margin. The transaction facts are a June 2026 amendment that extended maturities, and a July 2026 acquisition of Saxoprint and viaprinto that was funded from cash and the revolver and moved leverage higher. Governance is equity-oriented rather than sponsor-driven: management states that maximising intrinsic value per share is its uppermost objective and has repurchased shares every year in the periods supplied, but the filings document no priming, uptiering, dividend or debt-funded distribution. On the evidence in the pack the behaviour category is Neutral or Mixed: transparent reporting and an extension of maturities beside steady repurchases and an unresolved acquisition funding plan. Ownership percentages, control rights and sponsor history are not supplied; the filing says about 70% of shares are held by the top 10 shareholders without naming them.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Saxoprint and viaprinto. On July 2, 2026 Cimpress acquired the Saxoprint and viaprinto businesses of CEWE Stiftung & Co. KGaA, a subsequent event to the FY2026 10-K period and part of Q1 FY2027. The September 2026 10-Q states total purchase consideration of $141,081 (US$141.1m; €123,996), funded in cash from the available cash balance and the senior secured revolving credit facility (10-Q Sep 2026 page:18). Business acquisitions net of cash acquired were 131,557 (10-Q Sep 2026 page:4) and revolver borrowings were 35,000 (page:21). The preliminary allocation records goodwill of 36,480, intangible assets of 22,471 in total, and assets held for sale of 46,449 (page:19); final values are expected in the second quarter of FY2027. The business is managed within PrintBrothers, and its revenue and earnings in the quarter are described as not material. The 10-K, written after closing, stated the price as €120,000 subject to a post-closing adjustment and said no definitive sale-leaseback agreement had been executed (10-K pages:70, 142); the 10-Q says a plan to market and execute a sale-leaseback of the manufacturing facility was approved in Q1 FY2027 and the asset is held for sale (10-Q Sep 2026 page:19). Status: closed; sale-leaseback planned, not evidenced as signed. Liquidity effect: cash fell from 248,851 to 120,127 over the quarter (CP-1).

Costs: debt issuance costs of 7,789 and a discount of 2,750 capitalised, and a loss on early extinguishment of 3,722 for FY2026 (10-K page:119). Status: executed and effective. The agreement itself is not supplied. At September 30, 2026 the Term Loan B was 1,094,500 and the revolver commitment 250,000 with 35,000 drawn (10-Q Sep 2026 page:21).

rows.label: Cimpress is a public, founder-led, non-sponsored web-to-print group. VistaPrint is the profit engine; capital allocation favours share repurchases, and a debt-funded European acquisition in July 2026 lifted leverage.
VistaPrint produced 61.1% of FY2026 segment EBITDA and about half of segment revenue; its margins are the highest in the group.
Profits are seasonal: the December quarter carries most annual earnings, and Q1 FY2027 adjusted EBITDA fell year on year.
The 7.375% notes due 2032 replaced the 7.0% notes due 2026 in FY2025, and the secured facility was extended in June 2026 to 2033 and 2031.
Share repurchases totalled US$284.8m across FY2024 to FY2026, with a further US$200m authorisation in March 2026, none used in Q1 FY2027.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Cimpress is a moderately leveraged, cash-generative high yield credit whose financial risk rose in the latest quarter because a debt-funded acquisition coincided with margin pressure. Its strongest support is the VistaPrint brand, which earned 61.1% of FY2026 segment EBITDA, together with USD 317.8 million of liquidity and small scheduled maturities until the notes and term loan fall due in 2032 and 2033. The weakest point is margin: adjusted EBITDA fell to USD 89.8 million in Q1 FY2027 from USD 98.7 million while total debt reached USD 1,667.6 million, or 3.71x trailing EBITDA. What decides the outcome is whether margins recover through the December peak season and whether cost actions and any sale-leaseback proceeds reduce net debt before the 2032 refinancing.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Cimpress's leverage rose in the latest quarter and is not yet pro forma for its acquisition. Total debt principal was USD 1,667.6 million at September 30, 2026, equal to 3.71x trailing adjusted EBITDA of USD 449.6 million, against 3.57x at FY2026, and net debt to EBITDA rose to 3.44x from 3.03x as cash fell from USD 248.9 million to USD 120.1 million. The July 2026 Saxoprint acquisition cost USD 131.6 million net of cash acquired and was funded from cash and a USD 35.0 million revolver drawing; trailing EBITDA holds only the post-closing contribution, which the filing calls not material, and acquired pre-closing EBITDA is not supplied [CP-1; CP-1A transaction summary]. This is documentary fact.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The earnings trend is the central weakness. Adjusted EBITDA was USD 89.8 million in Q1 FY2027 against USD 98.7 million a year earlier, with revenue up 8% to USD 934.1 million but only 2% on an organic constant-currency basis. Cost of revenue rose to 56.3% of revenue from 53.3% on start-up costs for the North American network, depreciation, tariffs and energy, partly offset by a USD 7.5 million tariff refund [CP-1A operating model]. Adjusted EBITDA also adds back USD 61.4 million of share-based compensation in FY2026; if that add-back is treated as a cost, total leverage at FY2026 is 4.12x rather than 3.57x [CP-1 calculations]. This is Analyst Interpretation built on documentary figures.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Earnings are concentrated. VistaPrint produced USD 392.6 million of USD 642.1 million segment EBITDA in FY2026, or 61.1%, with gross margin of about 55% (management's approximate figure) and low working capital because customers pay before production [CP-1A operating model]. The Upload and Print segments, at about 32% gross margin, drive growth and acquisitions but contribute less profit per revenue dollar. A fall in VistaPrint advertising efficiency or tariff costs would therefore move group EBITDA more than any other single factor.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Refinancing risk is distant but has a trigger. Scheduled amortisation is USD 11.5 million to USD 18.5 million a year and USD 1,570.6 million falls due after FY2031, mostly the USD 525.0 million 7.375% senior notes due September 15, 2032 and the term loan due June 4, 2033. The 10-Q adds that the term loan matures earlier, on June 16, 2032, if the notes have not been repaid, refinanced or extended, which the 10-K does not state; the credit agreement is not supplied to settle this [CP-1A conflicts log]. The practical maturity wall is therefore mid-2032.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Covenant protection is limited. The only maintenance covenant is a Consolidated Leverage Ratio not above 4.50x, tested only when revolving usage exceeds 20% of commitments at a quarter end; usage was 14.0% at September 30, 2026, so the test did not apply and management states compliance with all covenants. The reported covenant ratio and its EBITDA definition are not printed, so headroom cannot be calculated [CP-1]. Protection therefore rests on collateral for the secured facility and on incurrence and restricted-payment limits that are not visible in the supplied sources.

facts.text: Capital allocation is equity-oriented. Management states its uppermost objective is intrinsic value per share, repurchased USD 284.8 million of shares over FY2024 to FY2026 and authorised a further USD 200 million in March 2026, with none used in Q1 FY2027 [CP-1A governance table]. No dividend, priming, uptiering or debt-funded distribution is documented, so the behaviour category is Neutral or Mixed rather than Extraction-Oriented or Creditor-Adverse, but legal capacity cannot be tested without the documents.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Cimpress has a profitable, cash-collected flagship in VistaPrint, which serves about 11 million small businesses a year with an average order value of about USD 100 and produced 61.1% of FY2026 segment EBITDA, so revenue visibility rests on a very large number of small orders rather than a few customers [CP-1A operating model; Documentary Fact, with the order-value figures as Management Language]. It has maintained cash interest cover of 4.11x and positive adjusted free cash flow of USD 130.9 million over the trailing twelve months despite lower margins [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. It refinanced the 2026 notes with 2032 notes in FY2025 and extended the secured facility to 2033 and 2031 in June 2026, which leaves no sizeable scheduled maturity for several years [CP-1A transaction summary; Documentary Fact]. Liquidity of USD 317.8 million and a revolver only 14.0% drawn leave room under the springing covenant [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. Disclosure is transparent, with reconciliations of adjusted EBITDA and adjusted free cash flow [CP-1A; Documentary Fact].

facts.text: Weaknesses. Leverage of 3.71x total and 3.44x net on issuer-defined EBITDA is rising, and 4.12x if share-based compensation is treated as a cost [CP-1; Analyst Interpretation]. Margins are under pressure from tariffs, energy, depreciation and plant start-up, and Q1 FY2027 adjusted EBITDA is lower than a year ago despite an acquisition [CP-1A operating model; Documentary Fact]. Earnings are concentrated in one brand and one quarter [CP-1A; Documentary Fact]. Ownership percentages and control rights are not disclosed beyond a statement that the top 10 holders own about 70% [CP-1A company profile; Insufficient Information].

The financial base is adequate for downstream credit work, with stated limits. Reported statements for FY2024, FY2025, FY2026, Q1 FY2026 and Q1 FY2027 are complete and their expense blocks reconcile to operating income. Weighted-average rate on borrowings under the Restated Credit Agreement was 5.89% including swaps (10-Q Sep 2026 page:22). Variable-rate debt was 1,129.5 million, interest rate swaps accruing interest had a notional of 350,000 thousand, and a 100 basis point rise would add 7.4 million to interest expense over twelve months (10-Q Sep 2026 pages:13, 50).
### Credit interpretation

- Leverage and acquisition effect. Between June 30, 2026 and September 30, 2026 debt principal rose by 31,227 thousand while cash fell by 128,724 thousand, because Saxoprint cost 131,557 thousand net of cash acquired and was funded from cash and 35,000 thousand of revolver borrowings (10-Q Sep 2026 pages:4, 21). Net leverage therefore rose to 3.44x from 3.03x, while LTM EBITDA holds only the post-acquisition part of the new business and its pre-acquisition EBITDA is not supplied. The first-quarter adjusted EBITDA decline (89,820 against 98,715) came mainly from higher start-up costs for the North American network, tariff costs and depreciation, partly offset by a 7.5 million tariff refund benefit (10-Q Sep 2026 page:33). Run-rate leverage after acquired EBITDA and any sale-leaseback proceeds cannot be derived from the sources.

- Quality of EBITDA. Issuer adjusted EBITDA adds back share-based compensation (61,379 in FY2026, 13.4% of FY2026 adjusted EBITDA) and deducts realised losses on currency hedges (14,169). Treating share-based compensation as a cost gives FY2026 EBITDA of 397,119 and total leverage of 4.12x; on LTM figures 387,106 and 4.31x. The hedge programme targets adjusted EBITDA to maintain stability on debt covenants (10-Q Sep 2026 page:50), so adjusted EBITDA is plausibly close to the covenant definition, but that cannot be confirmed without the credit agreement.

- Cash generation. Operating cash flow fell from 350,722 (FY2024) to 283,706 (FY2026) while capital spending, including capitalised software, rose to 167,290 in FY2026. Issuer adjusted free cash flow, which is after cash interest because operating cash flow includes interest paid (10-Q Sep 2026 page:34), fell from 261,053 to 122,432. In FY2026 cash was also used for acquisitions of 32,390, share repurchases of 50,077, withholding taxes on equity awards of 19,313 and finance lease payments of 11,740 (10-K pages:89-90). A buyback authorisation of 200 million remains (10-Q Sep 2026 page:52); none was used in Q1 FY2027, and share repurchases are restricted payments under the secured facility (10-Q Sep 2026 page:21).

- Liquidity. Liquidity at September 30, 2026 was 317.8 million against 481.6 million at June 30, 2026. Contractual obligations falling due within one year total 278,887 thousand including interest, leases and purchase commitments (10-Q Sep 2026 page:45). The second fiscal quarter is the peak season; the first-quarter working capital outflow was 23.7 million (10-Q Sep 2026 page:44).

- Maturities and refinancing. Scheduled amortisation is small (11.5 to 18.5 million a year), with 1,570.6 million due after FY2031. The Term Loan B springs to June 16, 2032 unless the 2032 Notes are repaid, refinanced or extended, so the practical wall is the 525.0 million note refinancing in 2032.

- Debt-like claims outside the debt figure. Finance leases of 56,003, operating lease payments of 157,858 (undiscounted fixed), supply chain finance of 58,781 inside accounts payable, purchase commitments of 310,257 (cloud services 192,636), redeemable noncontrolling interests of 78,361 (a put exercised by minority holders of one small business will require 9,602 in the second quarter of FY2027), and pension liabilities of 9,060. Including finance leases, total leverage is 3.83x on LTM figures. Book equity is a deficit of 479,409 after cumulative share repurchases (treasury shares at cost 1,363,550).

- Covenant. A maintenance test of Consolidated Leverage Ratio not above 4.50x applies only if revolving loans, swingline loans and unreimbursed letter of credit disbursements exceed 20% of commitments at a fiscal quarter end (10-Q Sep 2026 page:21). On the printed 35,000 of loans against 250,000 of commitments, usage was 14.0%, so the test was not triggered at September 30, 2026; 15,000 of further drawings would reach the 20% threshold. Management states compliance with all covenants (10-Q Sep 2026 page:21). The covenant ratio itself is not printed.

- Data checks. Operating income reconciles to gross profit less the expense block of technology, marketing, general and administrative, intangible amortisation and restructuring for all five periods. The adjusted EBITDA bridges recompute to the printed figures. Debt principal by instrument sums to the printed total at each date.

Issuer: CIMPRESS plc (Cimpress plc, Irish-incorporated parent of the Cimpress group; Nasdaq ticker CMPR). As-of date and cutoff: 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit_snapshot. Current period Q1 FY2027 (three months ended September 30, 2026); prior period FY2026 (year ended June 30, 2026). Reporting currency USD.

Question: which transaction, business, ownership and operating facts matter most to a creditor, and what do they imply for business risk, cash conversion, liquidity, refinancing, governance and creditor control? Scope is the pinned filings only. Sources are filings (10-K, three 10-Qs); the three earnings-release exhibits hold no readable content (CP-0). Management characterisations are quoted or tagged Management Language and are never adopted. No peer ranking, instrument recommendation or expected recovery outcome is given. Financial figures are those of the CP-1 financial base; business figures are quoted from the cited page.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Cimpress is a public, founder-led, non-sponsored web-to-print group. VistaPrint is the profit engine; capital allocation favours share repurchases, and a debt-funded European acquisition in July 2026 lifted leverage. | Medium | Ownership percentages, customer concentration and the legal documents are not supplied; the earnings releases are unreadable. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| VistaPrint produced 61.1% of FY2026 segment EBITDA and about half of segment revenue; its margins are the highest in the group. | Earnings and cash flow depend on one small-business brand, so advertising costs and tariffs there drive debt service capacity. | High |

| Profits are seasonal: the December quarter carries most annual earnings, and Q1 FY2027 adjusted EBITDA fell year on year. | Liquidity is thinnest in the first half of the fiscal year, when working capital is built before peak season. | High |

| The 7.375% notes due 2032 replaced the 7.0% notes due 2026 in FY2025, and the secured facility was extended in June 2026 to 2033 and 2031. | No near-term refinancing wall, but the term loan springs to June 16, 2032 unless the notes are refinanced. | High |

| Share repurchases totalled US$284.8m across FY2024 to FY2026, with a further US$200m authorisation in March 2026, none used in Q1 FY2027. | Management targets intrinsic value per share, not deleveraging, so debt reduction is not a stated priority. | Medium |

| The Saxoprint purchase (US$141.1m) was funded from cash and the revolver, with a planned sale-leaseback not yet evidenced as agreed. | Net leverage rose; any sale-leaseback proceeds would offset part of the outflow but are unconfirmed. | Medium |
### Business and transaction view

Cimpress is a decentralised group of web-to-print and promotional-product businesses run by a small central team, financed with a covenant-light structure of a secured term loan and revolver plus unsecured notes. The creditor-relevant business facts are that one brand, VistaPrint, supplies most segment EBITDA with high gross margin and low working capital; that the Upload and Print segments earn lower margins but are growing faster and are the acquisition platform; that profits are concentrated in the December quarter; and that U.S. tariffs, energy and North American capacity start-up costs are compressing margin. The transaction facts are a June 2026 amendment that extended maturities, and a July 2026 acquisition of Saxoprint and viaprinto that was funded from cash and the revolver and moved leverage higher. Governance is equity-oriented rather than sponsor-driven: management states that maximising intrinsic value per share is its uppermost objective and has repurchased shares every year in the periods supplied, but the filings document no priming, uptiering, dividend or debt-funded distribution. On the evidence in the pack the behaviour category is Neutral or Mixed: transparent reporting and an extension of maturities beside steady repurchases and an unresolved acquisition funding plan. Ownership percentages, control rights and sponsor history are not supplied; the filing says about 70% of shares are held by the top 10 shareholders without naming them.
### Company and operating model

| Revenue model | E-commerce self-service orders, plus Upload and Print sales to graphic professionals; digital and design services are a small share | Documentary Fact | 10-K pages:12, 14; 10-Q Sep 2026 page:35 | Orders are paid before production in VistaPrint, so cash conversion is favourable there |

Segment EBITDA total 133,848, of which VistaPrint 80,658 | Documentary Fact | 10-Q Sep 2026 pages:25, 27, 40 | Revenue growth of 8% was largely acquired (57.3 million from recent acquisitions); organic constant-currency growth was 2% |

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Saxoprint and viaprinto. On July 2, 2026 Cimpress acquired the Saxoprint and viaprinto businesses of CEWE Stiftung & Co. KGaA, a subsequent event to the FY2026 10-K period and part of Q1 FY2027. The September 2026 10-Q states total purchase consideration of $141,081 (US$141.1m; €123,996), funded in cash from the available cash balance and the senior secured revolving credit facility (10-Q Sep 2026 page:18). Business acquisitions net of cash acquired were 131,557 (10-Q Sep 2026 page:4) and revolver borrowings were 35,000 (page:21). The preliminary allocation records goodwill of 36,480, intangible assets of 22,471 in total, and assets held for sale of 46,449 (page:19); final values are expected in the second quarter of FY2027. The business is managed within PrintBrothers, and its revenue and earnings in the quarter are described as not material. The 10-K, written after closing, stated the price as €120,000 subject to a post-closing adjustment and said no definitive sale-leaseback agreement had been executed (10-K pages:70, 142); the 10-Q says a plan to market and execute a sale-leaseback of the manufacturing facility was approved in Q1 FY2027 and the asset is held for sale (10-Q Sep 2026 page:19). Status: closed; sale-leaseback planned, not evidenced as signed. Liquidity effect: cash fell from 248,851 to 120,127 over the quarter (CP-1).

Credit agreement amendment and restatement, June 4, 2026. The Restated Credit Agreement increased the Term Loan B by 35,289 to cover fees and increase liquidity, issued at 99.75% of par, extended the term loan to June 2033 and the revolver to June 2031, with no other material changes (10-K page:118). Costs: debt issuance costs of 7,789 and a discount of 2,750 capitalised, and a loss on early extinguishment of 3,722 for FY2026 (10-K page:119). Status: executed and effective. The agreement itself is not supplied. At September 30, 2026 the Term Loan B was 1,094,500 and the revolver commitment 250,000 with 35,000 drawn (10-Q Sep 2026 page:21).

7.375% Senior Notes due 2032. Issued under an indenture dated September 26, 2024 with certain subsidiaries as guarantors (10-K page:147); FY2025 proceeds of 525,000 and payments for early redemption or purchase of 7.0% Senior Notes due 2026 of 522,135 (10-K page:89; FY2025 column). Debt issuance costs of 11,658 were capitalised in FY2025 (10-K page:119). The notes are unsecured, pay semi-annual coupons on March 15 and September 15, and are redeemable at the indenture's prices (10-Q Sep 2026 pages:22, 47). Use of proceeds: refinancing of the 2026 notes, per the cash flow lines; the offering document is not supplied.

PrintBrothers minority sale, FY2026. A minority 8.75% interest in each PrintBrothers business was sold to members of management for cash of 24,814 (€21,000), with a 10-year lock-up and a put right from 2036; the redeemable interest was recorded at fair value 61,498 (€53,000), with a share-based compensation asset of 36,684 (10-K page:131). This adds a long-dated equity-like claim that can become a cash call from 2036; it also shows funding of the business from management, not from lenders.

Subsequent put exercise. Minority holders of one smaller business exercised a put; the purchase of their shares will cost 9,602 in Q2 FY2027 (10-Q Sep 2026 page:24). Status: committed, not yet paid at September 30, 2026.

Prior debt in the period: Q1 FY2027 borrowings of 100,848 and repayments of 69,529 (10-Q Sep 2026 page:5), consistent with the revolver draw and term loan amortisation. No new bond issue, rating action, or exchange offer is reported after June 30, 2026 within the supplied filings; the earnings releases that might describe later events are unreadable. Nothing after 2026-11-05 is used.
### Governance and capital allocation

Scope is the fundamental credit view, built from the financial base and the business and transaction context of the pinned filings (10-K for FY2026 and three 10-Qs, latest for Q1 FY2027). Peer ranking, instrument recommendation and recovery conclusions are out of scope.
## Sources

| EX-99.1_2026-04-29_q3_fy26quarterlyearnings.htm.jsonl | a3c79968ecfa051f20fab57025394eb1344a953bc437c701ec4c06c5f40daff7 | Header line only; no content used |

| EX-99.1_2026-10-28_q1_fy27quarterlyearnings.htm.jsonl | 68106c8dfde50a0adfff0c65c56bcc6710e9d79d49953b8ae58fdbbcc7a5502c | Header line only; no content used |
### Handoffs relied on
| Module | sha256 | Use |
| CP-0 | 2a472d32687bbe2e9753f148c731ca723b6cc01fbced782794d7008fa94ba154 | Source readiness and carried limitations |
| CP-1 | 9e1fc8f0f97240969fffa2c1f742f5f1ca2be5257610ee2a00f548b8773a3c57 | Financial base: leverage, cover, liquidity, maturities, debt detail |
| CP-1A | 8af7e402e1ee554a279562ddbbb7dc09f10da1dec1c068eb8c8ed46d58d4fdf4 | Business, ownership, transaction, governance and conflicts log |
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Cimpress is a moderately leveraged, cash-generative credit whose leverage rose to 3.71x after a debt-funded acquisition while margins weakened. Liquidity of USD 317.8 million and a distant refinancing date support it. | Medium | EBITDA is issuer-defined, and the covenant definitions, legal documents and ownership detail are not supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Total debt was USD 1,667.6 million at September 30, 2026, 3.71x trailing adjusted EBITDA, against 3.57x at FY2026. | Leverage is higher after the Saxoprint purchase and does not yet include acquired earnings. | High |
| Adjusted EBITDA fell to USD 89.8 million in Q1 FY2027 from USD 98.7 million, and cost of revenue rose to 56.3% of revenue. | Margin compression is the main threat to debt service capacity. | High |
| VistaPrint produced 61.1% of FY2026 segment EBITDA. | One brand carries most of the earnings that service the debt. | High |

| Liquidity was USD 317.8 million, down from USD 481.6 million at June 30, 2026, and most debt falls due after FY2031. | Near-term refinancing risk is low; the 2032 notes and term loan are the real maturity test. | High |

| Repurchases totalled USD 284.8 million over FY2024 to FY2026 and a new USD 200 million authorisation exists. | Capital allocation favours shareholders; restricted-payment limits are not visible. | Medium |
### Credit view

Cimpress is a moderately leveraged, cash-generative high yield credit whose financial risk rose in the latest quarter because a debt-funded acquisition coincided with margin pressure. Its strongest support is the VistaPrint brand, which earned 61.1% of FY2026 segment EBITDA, together with USD 317.8 million of liquidity and small scheduled maturities until the notes and term loan fall due in 2032 and 2033. The weakest point is margin: adjusted EBITDA fell to USD 89.8 million in Q1 FY2027 from USD 98.7 million while total debt reached USD 1,667.6 million, or 3.71x trailing EBITDA. What decides the outcome is whether margins recover through the December peak season and whether cost actions and any sale-leaseback proceeds reduce net debt before the 2032 refinancing.
### Credit assessment
| Element | Content | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Fundamental credit view | Moderate leverage with adequate liquidity; direction of risk is up in the latest quarter, driven by acquisition funding and margin compression | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 leverage, cover, liquidity and maturity tables; CP-1A operating model, transaction summary and conflicts log |

| Thesis | Cimpress can service its USD 1,667.6 million of debt from VistaPrint-led cash flow with no near-term maturity pressure, but its tolerance for further leverage or shareholder distributions is limited while margins are falling | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | Same |

| Confidence limits | Confidence is below High because the upstream handoffs record unsupplied covenant definitions, unsupplied legal documents, unreadable earnings releases, undisclosed ownership percentages and two unresolved conflicts | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-0 gaps; CP-1A gaps and conflicts log |
### Key findings

Cimpress's leverage rose in the latest quarter and is not yet pro forma for its acquisition. Total debt principal was USD 1,667.6 million at September 30, 2026, equal to 3.71x trailing adjusted EBITDA of USD 449.6 million, against 3.57x at FY2026, and net debt to EBITDA rose to 3.44x from 3.03x as cash fell from USD 248.9 million to USD 120.1 million. The July 2026 Saxoprint acquisition cost USD 131.6 million net of cash acquired and was funded from cash and a USD 35.0 million revolver drawing; trailing EBITDA holds only the post-closing contribution, which the filing calls not material, and acquired pre-closing EBITDA is not supplied [CP-1; CP-1A transaction summary]. This is documentary fact.

The earnings trend is the central weakness. Adjusted EBITDA was USD 89.8 million in Q1 FY2027 against USD 98.7 million a year earlier, with revenue up 8% to USD 934.1 million but only 2% on an organic constant-currency basis. Cost of revenue rose to 56.3% of revenue from 53.3% on start-up costs for the North American network, depreciation, tariffs and energy, partly offset by a USD 7.5 million tariff refund [CP-1A operating model]. Adjusted EBITDA also adds back USD 61.4 million of share-based compensation in FY2026; if that add-back is treated as a cost, total leverage at FY2026 is 4.12x rather than 3.57x [CP-1 calculations]. This is Analyst Interpretation built on documentary figures.

Earnings are concentrated. VistaPrint produced USD 392.6 million of USD 642.1 million segment EBITDA in FY2026, or 61.1%, with gross margin of about 55% (management's approximate figure) and low working capital because customers pay before production [CP-1A operating model]. The Upload and Print segments, at about 32% gross margin, drive growth and acquisitions but contribute less profit per revenue dollar. A fall in VistaPrint advertising efficiency or tariff costs would therefore move group EBITDA more than any other single factor.

Cash generation has weakened but still covers interest. Adjusted free cash flow, which is after cash interest, was USD 122.4 million in FY2026 against USD 148.0 million in FY2025 and USD 261.1 million in FY2024, and USD 130.9 million on the trailing twelve months. EBITDA covered cash interest 4.11x on the trailing twelve months and 4.18x in FY2026 [CP-1 interest cover and metrics tables]. The interest burden is partly floating: USD 1,129.5 million of variable-rate debt means a 100 basis point rise would add USD 7.4 million to annual interest expense, with swaps on a USD 350.0 million notional already accruing [CP-1 facility terms].

Liquidity is adequate but seasonal. Cash plus undrawn revolver was USD 317.8 million at September 30, 2026 (USD 120.1 million cash and USD 197.7 million of revolver availability), down USD 163.7 million from USD 481.6 million at June 30, 2026 [CP-1 liquidity table]. The first quarter builds inventory and receivables ahead of the December peak, and the December quarter carries most annual profit [CP-1A operating model]. Obligations due within one year, including interest, leases and purchase commitments, were USD 278.9 million.

Refinancing risk is distant but has a trigger. Scheduled amortisation is USD 11.5 million to USD 18.5 million a year and USD 1,570.6 million falls due after FY2031, mostly the USD 525.0 million 7.375% senior notes due September 15, 2032 and the term loan due June 4, 2033. The 10-Q adds that the term loan matures earlier, on June 16, 2032, if the notes have not been repaid, refinanced or extended, which the 10-K does not state; the credit agreement is not supplied to settle this [CP-1A conflicts log]. The practical maturity wall is therefore mid-2032.

Covenant protection is limited. The only maintenance covenant is a Consolidated Leverage Ratio not above 4.50x, tested only when revolving usage exceeds 20% of commitments at a quarter end; usage was 14.0% at September 30, 2026, so the test did not apply and management states compliance with all covenants. The reported covenant ratio and its EBITDA definition are not printed, so headroom cannot be calculated [CP-1]. Protection therefore rests on collateral for the secured facility and on incurrence and restricted-payment limits that are not visible in the supplied sources.

Capital allocation is equity-oriented. Management states its uppermost objective is intrinsic value per share, repurchased USD 284.8 million of shares over FY2024 to FY2026 and authorised a further USD 200 million in March 2026, with none used in Q1 FY2027 [CP-1A governance table]. No dividend, priming, uptiering or debt-funded distribution is documented, so the behaviour category is Neutral or Mixed rather than Extraction-Oriented or Creditor-Adverse, but legal capacity cannot be tested without the documents.

Claims outside the reported debt figure add to effective leverage. Finance leases of USD 56.0 million, supply chain finance of USD 58.8 million within payables, unrecorded purchase commitments of USD 310.3 million, redeemable noncontrolling interests of USD 78.4 million and a USD 9.6 million put due in Q2 FY2027 sit outside the USD 1,667.6 million. Including finance leases, total leverage on the trailing twelve months is 3.83x [CP-1].
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Cimpress has a profitable, cash-collected flagship in VistaPrint, which serves about 11 million small businesses a year with an average order value of about USD 100 and produced 61.1% of FY2026 segment EBITDA, so revenue visibility rests on a very large number of small orders rather than a few customers [CP-1A operating model; Documentary Fact, with the order-value figures as Management Language]. It has maintained cash interest cover of 4.11x and positive adjusted free cash flow of USD 130.9 million over the trailing twelve months despite lower margins [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. It refinanced the 2026 notes with 2032 notes in FY2025 and extended the secured facility to 2033 and 2031 in June 2026, which leaves no sizeable scheduled maturity for several years [CP-1A transaction summary; Documentary Fact]. Liquidity of USD 317.8 million and a revolver only 14.0% drawn leave room under the springing covenant [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. Disclosure is transparent, with reconciliations of adjusted EBITDA and adjusted free cash flow [CP-1A; Documentary Fact].

Weaknesses. Leverage of 3.71x total and 3.44x net on issuer-defined EBITDA is rising, and 4.12x if share-based compensation is treated as a cost [CP-1; Analyst Interpretation]. Margins are under pressure from tariffs, energy, depreciation and plant start-up, and Q1 FY2027 adjusted EBITDA is lower than a year ago despite an acquisition [CP-1A operating model; Documentary Fact]. Earnings are concentrated in one brand and one quarter [CP-1A; Documentary Fact]. Capital allocation prioritises repurchases, with an unused USD 200 million authorisation, while restricted-payment baskets are unknown [CP-1A governance table; Documentary Fact for the history, Insufficient Information for the covenant capacity]. The structure has a springing term loan maturity in 2032 tied to the notes, an unresolved acquisition price and sale-leaseback status, and significant debt-like claims outside reported debt [CP-1A conflicts log; Documentary Fact]. Ownership percentages and control rights are not disclosed beyond a statement that the top 10 holders own about 70% [CP-1A company profile; Insufficient Information].
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Risk mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Margin compression | Tariffs, energy, depreciation and North American plant start-up costs raise cost of revenue faster than pricing; the tariff refund benefit may not recur | Adjusted EBITDA falls, leverage rises above 3.71x and interest cover narrows from 4.11x | Material |

| Brand concentration | VistaPrint supplies 61.1% of segment EBITDA and depends on advertising efficiency and search traffic | A shortfall at one brand reduces debt service capacity disproportionately | Material |

| Acquisition-funded leverage | Saxoprint funded from cash and the revolver; acquired EBITDA and sale-leaseback proceeds unconfirmed | Net leverage 3.44x rises further if proceeds do not arrive; liquidity falls to USD 317.8 million | Material |

| Refinancing in 2032 | Notes of USD 525.0 million due September 15, 2032 and a term loan that springs to June 16, 2032 if the notes are not refinanced | A market-access test concentrated in mid-2032; floating-rate exposure of USD 1,129.5 million affects the cost | Material |

| Shareholder distributions | Equity-oriented objective, USD 284.8 million of repurchases and an unused USD 200 million authorisation | Cash that could reduce debt may be distributed; capacity under restricted-payment covenants unknown | Material |

| Information gaps | Covenant EBITDA, ratio, legal documents, guarantor list and ownership not supplied | Headroom, collateral priority and control cannot be tested; monitoring posture is restricted | Material |
| Seasonal liquidity trough | Working capital builds in the first half of the fiscal year before peak-season earnings | Liquidity can be tight if the December quarter underperforms | Minor |
| Debt-like claims outside debt | Finance leases, supply chain finance, purchase commitments, redeemable minority interests | Effective leverage is higher than reported debt suggests | Minor |
## Calculations
| Calculation | Inputs | Result |
| Fall in liquidity since FY2026 | USD 481.551 million (June 30, 2026) less USD 317.827 million (September 30, 2026) [CP-1] | USD 163.724 million |
| Rise in net leverage | 3.44x less 3.03x [CP-1] | 0.41x |
| Rise in cost of revenue ratio | 56.3% less 53.3% of revenue, Q1 FY2027 against Q1 FY2026 [CP-1A] | 3.0 percentage points |
All other figures are taken from the upstream handoffs without recalculation.
## Gaps
| Gap | Why it matters and what it affects | Severity | Action |

| Covenant EBITDA, the reported Consolidated Leverage Ratio and First Lien Leverage Ratio are not supplied | Headroom and the pricing grid cannot be tested; affects the covenant finding | Material | Obtain the June 4, 2026 Restated Credit Agreement and a compliance certificate |

| Credit agreement, indenture and guarantor list are not supplied | Restricted-payment and incurrence capacity, collateral and guarantee coverage cannot be tested; affects the distribution and priority findings | Material | Obtain the exhibits listed in the 10-K |
| Earnings releases are unreadable | No guidance or outlook; the Canva contribution is unquantified; affects margin outlook | Material | Re-extract the exhibits |
| Ownership percentages and control rights not disclosed in the supplied sources | Alignment and change-of-control exposure cannot be assessed | Material | Obtain the 2026 Proxy Statement |

| Pre-acquisition Saxoprint earnings, final allocation and sale-leaseback status; Saxoprint price and sale-leaseback conflict between the 10-K and the 10-Q is logged, not reconciled | Run-rate leverage and net acquisition cost unknown | Material | Monitor the next quarterly report, which is after the cutoff |

| Term loan final maturity differs between the 10-K and the 10-Q (June 4, 2033 against an earlier June 16, 2032 trigger); logged, not reconciled | Refinancing timing | Material | Read the credit agreement |

| Debt maturities by year at September 30, 2026 and June 30, 2024 debt are not printed; June 2025 revolver availability not supplied | Maturity chart uses the June 30, 2026 schedule | Minor | Use as labelled |
| Customer concentration, dividend history, ratings, quotes and peer data are not supplied | Revenue visibility and market-implied view limited | Minor | Not supplied |
## Next module

Pass to CP-5 for the evidence trace. Carry forward: leverage of 3.71x total and 3.44x net on issuer-defined adjusted EBITDA, 4.12x after treating share-based compensation as a cost at FY2026; liquidity of USD 317.8 million; 61.1% of FY2026 segment EBITDA from VistaPrint; the springing 4.50x covenant not triggered at 14.0% usage; the two logged conflicts (Saxoprint price and sale-leaseback status, term loan springing maturity); and the unsupplied covenant definitions, legal documents, ownership detail and earnings-release content. No peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion is given.

### Evidence trace view

The analysis is traceable enough for a fundamental credit snapshot, but not for covenant, priority or ownership conclusions. The debt, cash, adjusted EBITDA, liquidity, maturity and segment-profit figures that the four upstream handoffs rely on tie to filed statements and recompute without difference, so the gaps are source gaps, not unsupported claims. The most important provenance gap is the absence of the credit agreement and indenture, which leaves covenant EBITDA, headroom and restricted-payment capacity untestable. Several minor defects need plain correction downstream, led by leverage computed on debt principal rather than carrying value (3.66x against 3.71x on the trailing twelve months) and a rounding slip in the net leverage change (0.42x, not 0.41x). The credit conclusion is unchanged.
